title: Two Players Take the Smallest
statement:
Two players, Ada and Ben, play with an array nums of even length and an empty list result. They repeat rounds until nums is empty. In each round:

  1. Ada removes the smallest value left in nums.
  2. Then Ben removes the smallest value left in nums.
  3. Then Ben appends his value to result, and after that Ada appends hers.

Return result.

examples.why: Round 1: Ada takes 2, Ben takes 3, and Ben writes first: 3, 2. Round 2: Ada takes 4, Ben takes 5: 5, 4.
Both take a 1. The swap is invisible when the values are equal.
In sorted order the values are 1, 4, 4, 6, 9, 9. Each round takes the next two, written larger first.

hints: Each round takes the two smallest values left. In what overall order are values removed?
Values come out in ascending order, two per round. A min-heap simulates this directly; sorting once does too.
Sort ascending, then swap each pair: positions 0 and 1, 2 and 3, and so on.

explain.intuition:
"Repeatedly take the smallest" is what a min-heap is for: pop twice per round, append Ben's (the second pop) then Ada's (the first). That simulates the game exactly in O(n log n).

Then notice what the simulation really does. The heap hands out values in sorted order, so the whole game is: sort the array and write each consecutive pair in reverse. When all removals are known up front, a single sort replaces the heap. A heap earns its keep only when new values arrive between removals, like tasks being queued while a scheduler is running.
steps: Sort a copy of nums in ascending order.
For i = 0, 2, 4, …, swap the values at i and i + 1.
pitfalls: Appending Ada's value first. Ben, who took the larger value, writes first.
Sorting with JavaScript's default sort(), which compares as strings: [10, 2, 30, 2] would sort as 10, 2, 2, 30.
Finding the minimum with a fresh scan every time, which is O(n²) for 100 000 values.

solutions.title: Simulate with repeated scans
solutions.idea: Follow the rules literally: scan for the minimum, remove it, twice per round.

solutions.title: Min-heap simulation
solutions.idea: A min-heap gives the smallest remaining value in O(log n). Pop twice per round and append in Ben-then-Ada order.

solutions.title: Sort and swap pairs
solutions.idea: The values leave in sorted order two at a time, so sort once and reverse each consecutive pair.

followups: New values are added to nums between rounds. Which of the three solutions still works, and why?
Values are bounded by 100 000. How would counting sort make this O(n + max)?
